comment: Curated failures: model output next to the compiler or test output that rejected it. Real entries are cut from harness artifacts (model output is ours; surrounding context comes from the permissively-licensed upstream projects, never from the benchmark's curated task files). THESE ENTRIES ARE INVENTED SAMPLE DATA -- plausible, not observed.

entries.title: Clones, then returns a reference to the clone
entries.takeaway: Python's `return self.pubkey` has no lifetime. The model reproduced the shape, added a defensive `.clone()`, and handed back a pointer to a value that dies at the closing brace.
entries.compiler_error:
error[E0515]: cannot return reference to local variable `key`
   --> identity/src/ecdsa.rs:214:5
    |
214 |     &key
    |     ^^^^ returns a reference to data owned by the current function

For more information about this error, try `rustc --explain E0515`.
error: could not compile `libp2p-identity` (lib) due to 1 previous error

entries.title: Holds a read of `self` across a write to `self`
entries.takeaway: The Python original walks a list while updating `self.matches` in the same loop. That is free in Python and illegal in Rust: the immutable borrow from `best_match()` is still live at the push.
entries.compiler_error:
error[E0502]: cannot borrow `self.matches` as mutable because `*self` is also borrowed as immutable
   --> src/entity.rs:341:13
    |
338 |         let best = self.best_match();
    |                    ---- immutable borrow occurs here
...
341 |             self.matches.push(m.clone());
    |             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ mutable borrow occurs here
...
347 |         best.chaos()
    |         ---- immutable borrow later used here

For more information about this error, try `rustc --explain E0502`.

entries.title: Iterates a `Vec` by value, then asks for its length
entries.takeaway: `for addr in addrs` consumes the vector. Every small model in the sweep hit some form of this: Python names survive the loop, Rust bindings do not.
entries.compiler_error:
error[E0382]: borrow of moved value: `addrs`
   --> swarm/src/behaviour/peer_addresses.rs:96:26
    |
88  | pub fn add_addresses(&mut self, peer: &PeerId, addrs: Vec<Multiaddr>) -> bool {
    |                                                ----- move occurs because `addrs` has type `Vec<Multiaddr>`, which does not implement the `Copy` trait
...
91  |     for addr in addrs {
    |                 ----- `addrs` moved due to this implicit call to `.into_iter()`
...
96  |     self.prune(peer, addrs.len());
    |                      ^^^^^^^^^^ value borrowed here after move
    |
help: consider iterating over a slice of the `Vec<Multiaddr>`'s content to avoid moving into the `for` loop
    |
91  |     for addr in &addrs {
    |                 +

For more information about this error, try `rustc --explain E0382`.

entries.title: `as_i64()` where the struct wanted an `i32`
entries.takeaway: Python has one integer type. The dependency block showed `spec_id: i32`; the model still reached for serde_json's `as_i64` and shorthand-initialised the field.
entries.compiler_error:
error[E0308]: mismatched types
   --> crates/iceberg/src/spec/partition.rs:188:9
    |
188 |         spec_id,
    |         ^^^^^^^ expected `i32`, found `i64`
    |
help: you can convert an `i64` to an `i32` and panic if the converted value doesn't fit
    |
188 |         spec_id: spec_id.try_into().unwrap(),
    |                         ++++++++++++++++++++

For more information about this error, try `rustc --explain E0308`.

entries.title: Invented a dependency that is not in the workspace
entries.takeaway: The prompt ships the exact `use` block the target file has. The model added `itertools` anyway because it is the idiomatic way to write this in isolation. Repository-level translation punishes exactly this.
entries.compiler_error:
error[E0432]: unresolved import `itertools`
  --> crates/iceberg/src/scan.rs:24:5
   |
24 | use itertools::Itertools;
   |     ^^^^^^^^^ use of unresolved module or unlinked crate `itertools`
   |
   = help: if you wanted to use a crate named `itertools`, use `cargo add itertools` to add it to your `Cargo.toml`

For more information about this error, try `rustc --explain E0432`.

entries.title: `?` on an error type the crate cannot convert from
entries.takeaway: Survived the repair round. Shown the first error, the model rewrote the body but kept the bare `?` -- the crate deliberately has no `From<serde_json::Error>`, and nothing in the prompt says so.
entries.compiler_error:
error[E0277]: `?` couldn't convert the error to `iceberg::Error`
   --> crates/catalog/glue/src/catalog.rs:274:71
    |
274 |     let metadata: TableMetadata = serde_json::from_slice(&content)?;
    |                                                                    ^ the trait `From<serde_json::Error>` is not implemented for `iceberg::Error`
    |
    = note: the question mark operation (`?`) implicitly performs a conversion on the error value using the `From` trait
    = help: the following other types implement trait `From<T>`:
              `iceberg::Error` implements `From<opendal::Error>`
              `iceberg::Error` implements `From<std::io::Error>`

For more information about this error, try `rustc --explain E0277`.

entries.title: Compiles cleanly. Inverts the answer on the None case.
entries.takeaway: The interesting failure mode of the strongest models: rustc is happy, the borrow checker is happy, and the semantics quietly drifted. Only a real test suite catches this -- which is the whole argument for running the project's own tests.
